\title{When the Light Goes Out: Silent and Visible Failure\\of SLAM on a Ground Robot}

\author{\IEEEauthorblockN{Elias Bitsch}

\begin{abstract}
% No citations, symbols, maths or footnotes.
A robot that knows it is lost can stop; one that trusts a wrong pose keeps driving. We therefore ask whether SLAM failure is visible when the light is switched off. Two monocular systems built on 3D foundation models, VGGT-Long and MASt3R-SLAM, and \todo{the systems of the other members} run on three indoor sequences of a public ground-robot dataset with motion-capture ground truth and a LiDAR reference map. In normal light VGGT-Long is the more accurate foundation-model system. When the light switches on and off, it still reports a pose for every frame, logs no error and ends two metres off, while MASt3R-SLAM stops, logs more than a thousand failed relocalisations and stays three times closer to the truth. The confidence of the underlying model drops to its lowest possible value in the dark, but the pipeline does not act on it. Code, configurations and results are public.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}
Service robots move through rooms where lights are switched on and off. A camera-based system is expected to degrade in the dark; what matters for safety is whether it notices. Failure detection is an open problem of robust SLAM~\cite{cadena2016past}, and learned trackers tend to replace explicit tracking loss by silent drift~\cite{thomas2026failure}. 3D foundation models now predict poses and dense geometry in one forward pass~\cite{wang2024dust3r,wang2025vggt} and are built into SLAM systems~\cite{deng2026vggtlong,murai2025mast3rslam}. On a real light on/off sequence we ask: \emph{(RQ1)} how accurate are trajectory and map in normal light, \emph{(RQ2)} how does each system fail in the dark, and \emph{(RQ3)} does the run show that it failed? Light is the stress test, not the finding. We contribute an evaluation of foundation-model SLAM under real illumination change with motion-capture ground truth, evidence and a mechanism for a silent failure, and an open pipeline.

\section{State of the Art}
SLAM is commonly posed as maximum-a-posteriori estimation over a factor graph~\cite{cadena2016past}. DUSt3R regresses dense point maps for image pairs~\cite{wang2024dust3r}; VGGT extends this to many images and outputs camera poses and depth maps without bundle adjustment~\cite{wang2025vggt}. VGGT-Long joins overlapping chunks of VGGT predictions with Sim(3) transforms estimated on the shared frames and closes loops in a Sim(3) pose graph~\cite{deng2026vggtlong}. MASt3R-SLAM tracks frames against keyframes with MASt3R matches, optimises a keyframe graph with loop closure and relocalises when tracking fails~\cite{murai2025mast3rslam}. With one camera, scale is unobservable~\cite{zhang2018tutorial}.
\stixSota\ \zhouSota\ \ovdiienkoSota

Robustness is often tested with synthetic perturbations~\cite{xu2024perturbation}, but a synthetic illumination change can reverse the ranking that real adverse conditions produce~\cite{thomas2026failure}. Under synthetic low light, MASt3R was rated robust by tracking success and ATE~\cite{kumar2026uavslam}, without asking whether a failure would be noticed. Introspective perception predicts the failures of vision systems~\cite{rabiee2020ivslam}. VGGT's per-pixel confidence is trained as aleatoric uncertainty~\cite{wang2025vggt,kendall2017uncertainties}; VGGT reports no pose uncertainty, and its confidence predicts pose failures only partly~\cite{srinivasan2026vggtknow}. 3D foundation models even produce consistent-looking geometry for random noise~\cite{paul2026onescene}. Whether the failure of foundation-model SLAM under a real loss of light is visible has not been studied.

\section{Materials and Methods}
\textbf{Dataset.} M3DGR~\cite{zhang2025m3dgr} is recorded with a wheeled robot carrying an RGB-D camera (RealSense D435i, $640\times480$, 30\,Hz), two Livox LiDARs, IMUs and wheel odometry; ground truth comes from motion capture at about 300\,Hz. We use three sequences in one $6.5\times3$\,m room: \emph{Dynamic01} (175\,s, 71\,m, people walking), \emph{Sha-turn01} (139\,s, 98\,m, sharp turns) and \emph{Varying-illu01} (154\,s, 72\,m, light off five times for 12 to 16\,s; 46\,\% of the frames have more than 80\,\% of their pixels below grey value 20).

\textbf{Systems.} All systems use the authors' default parameters. VGGT-Long (chunks of 60 frames, overlap 30, loop closure) runs on every third frame (10\,Hz), as its authors advise for dense input; MASt3R-SLAM runs on all frames. Both run on an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPU. \stixMethods\ \zhouMethods\ \ovdiienkoMethods

\textbf{Metrics.} We report the absolute trajectory error (ATE)~\cite{sturm2012benchmark}, computed with evo~\cite{grupp2017evo} after Umeyama alignment~\cite{umeyama1991least}, SE(3) for metric and Sim(3) for monocular systems~\cite{zhang2018tutorial}, as the median ATE RMSE over five runs, and the tracked fraction, the part of the ground-truth time covered by the estimate~\cite{campos2021orbslam3}. Maps are compared with a pseudo-ground truth built by stacking MID-360 scans along the motion-capture poses, with the marker-to-LiDAR offset chosen to make the cloud as sharp as possible~\cite{levinson2010unsupervised}; after alignment and ICP we report the F-score at 10\,cm~\cite{knapitsch2017tanks}. For RQ3 we record what each system reports itself: log messages, relocalisations and, for VGGT-Long, the mean depth confidence per frame, written out without changing the algorithm.

\textbf{RQ1, accuracy.} In normal light both systems track the whole sequence (Fig.~\ref{fig:traj}). VGGT-Long is about twice as accurate as MASt3R-SLAM (Tab.~\ref{tab:results}), but a lower ATE does not imply a better map: on \emph{Sha-turn01} MASt3R-SLAM's map scores higher. Five runs agree within 0.1\,mm except MASt3R-SLAM on \emph{Varying-illu01}; the spread over runs therefore says nothing about robustness.

Middle: chained scale of VGGT-Long's chunk links (left) and failed relocalisations of MASt3R-SLAM per second (right). Bottom: VGGT depth confidence; its lowest possible value is 1 (dotted).}
    \label{fig:timeline}
\end{figure*}

\textbf{RQ2, failure mode.} The systems fail in opposite ways (Fig.~\ref{fig:timeline}). VGGT-Long outputs a pose for every frame and ends at 2.35\,m ATE. Dark chunks are still joined to their neighbours, the chained chunk scale ends at 0.004 (0.52 and 0.55 on the lit sequences), and the whole trajectory shrinks towards the room centre; the error is even larger in lit frames (2.39\,m) than in dark ones (2.08\,m). MASt3R-SLAM stops adding keyframes in the dark and covers 83\,\% of the run; from the second dark phase on it fails to relocalise more than a thousand times, and its ATE stays at 0.69\,m. While relocalising, which runs in a separate thread, its runs end at either 0.63 or 0.69\,m.

\textbf{RQ3, detectability.} VGGT-Long's tracked fraction is 99.9\,\% on all sequences, including the failed one, and its log contains no error. MASt3R-SLAM's failure is visible as a gap in the trajectory and as failed relocalisations, which occur only on \emph{Varying-illu01}. Inside VGGT the signal exists: the depth confidence has a median of 4.6 in lit frames and sits at 1.00, its floor, in dark ones (95th percentile 1.16).

As a pipeline check, FAST-LIO2~\cite{xu2022fastlio2} reproduces the published M3DGR value on \emph{Dynamic01} (0.14 vs.\ 0.13\,m~\cite{zhang2025m3dgr}). Replacing VGGT with the metric MapAnything~\cite{keetha2025mapanything} misjudged the indoor scale by a factor of 3 to 10, and halving the chunks to fit a 16\,GB GPU raised the ATE on \emph{Sha-turn01} from 0.26 to 0.42\,m.

\section{Discussion and Outlook}
VGGT's confidence, although trained as aleatoric uncertainty~\cite{kendall2017uncertainties}, reaches its floor in the dark, so the model does mark these frames. VGGT-Long, however, only drops points below 10\,\% of the median confidence of the two chunks it joins. When both chunks are dark their points pass, the Sim(3) link is fitted to geometry hallucinated from black images~\cite{paul2026onescene}, and the scale error propagates along the chain. MASt3R-SLAM instead switches to relocalisation when too few matches are valid, which turns darkness into an explicit, logged state. This is the split between explicit failure and silent drift seen for other learned trackers~\cite{thomas2026failure}, and it shows that tracking success alone~\cite{kumar2026uavslam} can hide a failure. An absolute confidence check per chunk would expose VGGT-Long's failure; testing it and fusing wheel odometry or an IMU to bridge dark phases is future work.
\textbf{Limitations.} One dataset, room and light-change sequence give a documented case, not a general law. MASt3R-SLAM exports keyframes only, so its tracked fraction mixes keyframe density with tracking loss~\cite{thomas2026failure}. VGGT-Long runs at 10\,Hz, all systems use default parameters on different hardware, and the offset between motion-capture body and sensors is absorbed by the alignment, as in M3DGR~\cite{zhang2025m3dgr}.
